urls.description: In Cuba, the power grid collapsed again, leaving millions without power for the sixth time since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. Since then, just one tanker of fuel has been delivered by a Russian tanker in March. The blackouts have taken a heavy toll on Cubans, restricting transportation, shortening workdays, grounding flights and endangering public health. This is Valentin Parra, a resident of Havana. Valentin Parra: “It’s very bad for everyone, because everyone gets desperate in a house without water and without light. It’s a phenomenon that isn’t seen anywhere else in the world, only here. And when people don’t have water — look, I myself was without water for 15 days, without water or light for 15 days.”
urls.title: Power Grid Collapses in Cuba Again, Leaving Millions Without Power

Democrats enter the fall with their widest House generic-ballot lead of the year, according to the polling cited in this analysis: 49%-42% among voters and 53%-42% among likely voters.

But the path to a big Democratic night is not locked. Iran, DSA support and MAGA turnout could all affect how high the GOP ceiling goes.

The latest forecast gives Democrats 215 seats, with 19 toss-ups. Republicans still have narrow paths to hold the House as the race enters its final weeks.
